packet.headline_seed: Gina Rinehart calls for immigrants’ social media to be screened in Anzac memorial speech
packet.description_seed: Mining magnate also claims children are being taught to be ashamed of the Australian flag in a speech to 4,000 people on the Sydney Opera House steps Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australia’s richest person, Gina Rinehart, called for immigrants’ social media to be screened and said children are being taught to be ashamed of the Australian flag in untelevised remarks before an Anzac memorial service on the steps of Sydney Opera House on Friday. Rinehart’s public appearance was attended by about 4,000 people and sponsored by her company, Hancock Prospecting, and RSL New South Wales. Continue reading...
